plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches in late winter. It is widely cultivated in East Asian gardens and is celebrated in ume festivals, with flowers appearing before the leaves emerge.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Japan, China, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are a symbol of perseverance in East Asian culture because they bloom while snow may still be on the ground, often before cherry blossoms.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It carpets woodlands and gardens, pushing up through frost and sometimes snow.
plants.location: Europe, naturalized in the United Kingdom and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops contain galantamine, a compound used in medications to treat symptoms of early Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Australia's national floral emblem, a small tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, golden, fragrant flower balls. Its late-summer blooms bring bright color to Australian bushland as the southern hemisphere season shifts.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the wild, with some flowering extending across seasons depending on region
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1 in Australia, and the golden wattle's green and gold colors were adopted as the national sporting colors.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A bold shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, featuring a bowl of pink-tipped bracts surrounding a central cluster of florets. It thrives in the fynbos of South Africa and is grown in warm, dry gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer through spring depending on location, with peaks from late summer to early autumn
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower and can survive wildfires thanks to a woody underground lignotuber that resprouts after burning.
